title: Documenting technical solutions on Mac: a guide for IT support technicians
metaTitle: Documenting technical solutions on Mac: a guide for IT support technicians
description: Learn how to improve your knowledge base documentation as an IT support technician on macOS to save time, reduce ticket volume, and stop burnout.
intro: Documenting technical solutions is the most effective way to lower your daily ticket volume and prevent repetitive support requests. When you keep your knowledge base updated on your Mac, you stop wasting time solving the same issues over and over.
tldr: Poor documentation causes avoidable escalations, wasting thousands of dollars monthly.
Technicians lose over 30 minutes daily just searching for information.
Burnout increases when you lack the tools to document fixes efficiently.
Standardizing your workflow with templates and AI tools creates a sustainable system.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of poor documentation

When you fail at documenting technical solutions, the cost is not just your time. It is the cost of your entire team. Every time a user submits a ticket for an issue you already solved but never wrote down, you pay the price of a full support cycle.

A Level 1 ticket costs around $22. If you let 200 of these become avoidable escalations, you burn $12,400 a month. This is money that could go toward better tools or team growth. Instead, it vanishes into the void of repetitive manual labor.

The most common reason for bad documentation is a reactive culture. You are busy. A phone rings, a Slack message arrives, or a user walks up to your desk. You fix the issue and move to the next one. Writing the guide feels like a luxury you cannot afford.

items: Knowledge silos: You keep the fix in your head or a hidden text file.
Psychological depletion: Burnout makes you less willing to share what you know.
Disconnected systems: Your notes are in Apple Notes, but your tickets are in Jira.
Lack of templates: Starting from a blank page is too slow.

blocks.text: You do not need to buy new software to fix this. You need a better routine. Start by creating a standard template for every fix. Include the problem, the steps to reproduce it, and the final solution.

items: Create a text snippet for common resolutions. Use System Settings > Keyboard > Text Replacements.
Keep your documentation in a single app. If you use Notion or Confluence, stick to it.
Set aside 15 minutes at the end of every day to document one fix.
Use a single point of contact model for all your internal knowledge.

blocks.text: If you handle sensitive client or patient data, always follow your employer's rules regarding where and how you store technical documentation. Never put passwords or PII in a public-facing knowledge base.

blocks.text: Lazur works as your personal documentation assistant on your Mac. When you are fixing an issue, hold the key and describe what you are doing. Lazur drafts the steps for you while you work.
You can ask Lazur to draft a guide from your spoken notes. It turns your verbal explanation into a formatted, step-by-step document. You save time and ensure your team has the information they need.

faq.question: How do I stop burnout from documentation?
faq.answer: Stop treating it as a separate task. Document while you solve the issue. Use voice dictation to capture steps in real-time.

faq.question: Is it worth documenting every small issue?
faq.answer: If you solve it more than twice, write it down. The time you save on the third request pays for the time you spent writing the guide.

faq.question: Where should I store my technical guides?
faq.answer: Use a centralized tool like Notion, Confluence, or your company's internal wiki. Avoid storing knowledge in personal email or local text files.

costs.title: Escalation waste
costs.text: Every avoidable ticket costs your company money and wastes your time on low-level tasks.

costs.title: Refocus time
costs.text: Every time you stop to search for a fix you forgot, you lose over 20 minutes of momentum.

costs.title: Burnout
costs.text: The feeling of being stuck in a cycle of repetitive work is a primary driver of turnover.

causes.title: Reactive culture
causes.text: You prioritize the next ticket over documenting the last one because you are always behind.

causes.title: Knowledge silos
causes.text: Information stays in your head or in scattered files instead of a shared team repository.

causes.title: Lack of process
causes.text: There is no standard way to write a guide, so you avoid doing it entirely.

fixes.title: Standardize your template
fixes.text: Use a simple format for every guide: Problem, Environment, Steps, and Solution.

fixes.title: Build a snippet library
fixes.text: Use macOS Text Replacements to quickly insert common troubleshooting steps into your tickets.

fixes.title: End-of-day documentation
fixes.text: Block 15 minutes at the end of your shift to write down one solution from your day.
